subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Show that one value of [(1 + sin π/8 + i cos π/8)/(1 + sin π/8 − i cos π/8)]^(8/3) is −1.

mark_split.label: Let z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8 and find 1/z
Raise to 8/3 by De Moivre's theorem

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — what you call z, why the fraction is just z, how you write z in cis form, and what the 8/3 power does to the angle.
insider_note: The question looks long and is short: the fraction is z itself. Students who convert both brackets to mod-amp form separately run out of time.

steps.label: Let z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8 and find 1/z
steps.margin_note: First and second marks. Put z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8. Then 1/z = (sin π/8 − i cos π/8)/(sin² π/8 + cos² π/8) = sin π/8 − i cos π/8, so the number in the denominator is 1/z and the two brackets are 1 + z and 1 + 1/z.
steps.memory_tip: sin² + cos² = 1, so 1/z is simply sin π/8 − i cos π/8. The denominator's number is the reciprocal of the numerator's.
lines: Let z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8
= (sin π/8 − i cos π/8)/(sin² π/8 + cos² π/8)
= sin π/8 − i cos π/8  (∵ sin² θ + cos² θ = 1)

recall.must_convey: That the numerator's number is named z, and 1/z is its conjugate sin π/8 − i cos π/8 because its modulus is 1.
accept: let z be sin pi by eight plus i cos pi by eight, then one by z is the conjugate since the modulus is one
call the number z, its reciprocal is sin pi by eight minus i cos pi by eight
one over z equals the conjugate because sin squared plus cos squared is one
z ni sin pi by eight plus i cos pi by eight ga teeskunte one by z conjugate avuthundi
the denominator's number is exactly one by z

steps.why: The two brackets in the question are 1 + z and 1 + 1/z for the same z. Seeing that the denominator's number is the reciprocal of the numerator's is the idea of the whole question.
common_mistakes: Not noticing that sin π/8 − i cos π/8 is 1/z, and trying to write both brackets in mod-amp form separately.
Writing 1/z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8 with no sign change.
Leaving sin² π/8 + cos² π/8 in the denominator instead of replacing it by 1.

steps.label: The fraction simplifies to z
steps.margin_note: Third and fourth marks. 1 + 1/z = (z + 1)/z, so (1 + z) divided by it leaves z. The whole expression is z to the power 8/3 and nothing more.
steps.memory_tip: 1 + 1/z = (z + 1)/z, so (1 + z) divided by it leaves z. The whole expression is z^(8/3).

recall.must_convey: That (1 + z)/(1 + 1/z) simplifies to z, so the whole expression is z to the power 8/3.
accept: one plus z over one plus one by z is z, so the expression is z to the eight by three
multiply top and bottom by z and the fraction becomes z
the bracket simplifies to z so we need z power eight by three
fraction simplify cheste z matrame migulutundi, z power eight by three
one plus one by z is z plus one over z, and it cancels with the numerator
heard_as: z to the eight by three

steps.why: 1 + 1/z = (z + 1)/z, so dividing 1 + z by it leaves z. The long expression is z to the power 8/3 and nothing more.
common_mistakes: Cancelling the 1's and writing z/(1/z) = z², which is wrong algebra.
Expanding 1 + z with sines and cosines and making errors.
Forgetting to carry the 8/3 power onto z.

steps.label: Write z as cis 3π/8
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. z is written sine first, so use cos(π/2 − π/8) = sin π/8 and sin(π/2 − π/8) = cos π/8 to swap them: z = cos(3π/8) + i sin(3π/8). De Moivre needs the cosine first and the sine second.
steps.memory_tip: z is written sine first. Swap with cos(π/2 − π/8), so the angle becomes 3π/8.
lines: z = sin π/8 + i cos π/8

recall.must_convey: That sin π/8 = cos(π/2 − π/8) and cos π/8 = sin(π/2 − π/8), so z = cos 3π/8 + i sin 3π/8.
accept: sin pi by eight is cos of pi by two minus pi by eight so z is cos three pi by eight plus i sin three pi by eight
swap sin and cos using the complementary angle, z is cis three pi by eight
write z as cos three pi by eight plus i sin three pi by eight
sin ni cos ga marchali, pi by two minus pi by eight three pi by eight, z is cis three pi by eight
the amplitude of z is three pi by eight

steps.why: De Moivre's theorem needs cos first and sin second. z is written sin-first, so the complementary-angle identities swap the roles: the angle becomes π/2 − π/8 = 3π/8.
common_mistakes: Applying De Moivre directly to sin π/8 + i cos π/8, which is not in cos + i sin form.
Getting π/2 − π/8 = π/4 or 3π/4 instead of 3π/8.
Writing z = cis(π/8), ignoring the swap.

steps.label: Raise to 8/3 by De Moivre
steps.margin_note: Sixth and seventh marks. The angle becomes (8/3) · (3π/8) = π, so the value is cos π + i sin π = −1 + i(0). A fractional power has several values; this is the one the question asks for.
steps.memory_tip: (8/3) · (3π/8) = π, so the value is cos π + i sin π = −1.
lines: = cos π + i sin π = −1 + i(0)

lines.text: ∴ one value of the expression is −1

recall.must_convey: That one value of z to the 8/3 is cis((8/3)(3π/8)) = cis π = −1 by De Moivre's theorem.
accept: by De Moivre the angle is eight by three times three pi by eight which is pi, so cos pi plus i sin pi is minus one
multiply the angle by eight by three to get pi and cis pi is minus one
one value is cos pi plus i sin pi equals minus one
angle ni eight by three tho multiply cheste pi vasthundi, cis pi is minus one
the eight and the three cancel leaving pi, and cis pi is minus one

steps.why: The 8 and the 3 cancel against the 3π/8, leaving the angle π. cos π = −1 and sin π = 0, so this value of the power is −1. A fractional power has several values; the question asks for one, and De Moivre supplies it.
common_mistakes: Writing cos π + i sin π = 1.
Claiming −1 is the only value of the expression; the question says 'one value' for a reason.
